identity_notes: Per the coordinator's partition-level guidance, butterbur carries known safety literature (pyrrolizidine alkaloid hepatotoxicity) that is routed to the handoff safety owner rather than folded into efficacy conclusions here; efficacy records are kept and annotated but the identity_notes and handoff list both flag the hepatotoxicity concern prominently. Two distinct, well-separated evidence bodies exist: (1) MIGRAINE PROPHYLAXIS, where the proprietary root extract Petadolex has the strongest guideline-level support (AAN/AHS Level A recommendation, PMID 22529203; Canadian Headache Society strong recommendation, PMID 22683887) built on a small number of placebo-controlled RCTs (11020030, 14752215, 15623680) plus a systematic review of only 2 pooled trials (16987643, 293 patients total) -- the evidence base, while guideline-endorsed, rests on few trials, and one of the largest (15623680) found the 50 mg bid dose was NOT significantly better than placebo, only the 75 mg bid dose was; and (2) ALLERGIC RHINITIS/ASTHMA, where the standardized leaf extract Ze 339 has a larger and more consistent RCT base (11799030, 15611396, 16114089, 16751170) generally showing non-inferiority to antihistamines, but with at least one clean placebo-controlled negative trial (15281472) and a negative skin-test mechanistic trial (16784008, 16784008 comparator acrivastine WAS effective). A substantial share of retrieved 'positive' records for both indications are narrative reviews/guidelines that name butterbur among several other treatments without isolating a butterbur-specific quantitative result (flagged related_form_differs/combination throughout) -- reviewers should weight the small number of primary RCTs, not the large count of reviews that cite them. A distinct third evidence stream concerns the FIXED COMBINATION PRODUCT Ze 185 (butterbur + valerian + passionflower + lemon balm) for stress/somatoform/benzodiazepine-sparing indications (19274698, 29433687, 31985131) -- these are NOT evidence for single-ingredient butterbur and are flagged related_form_differs. Hepatotoxicity from pyrrolizidine alkaloids is the dominant safety theme across this identity (multiple independent sources) and is central to any handoff safety review; PA-free (CO2-extracted) processing is repeatedly cited as the mitigating factor.
